title: Runtime Instrumentation Catalog and Incident Playbook
author: Ethan Chu
content:
Summary

This page defines the canonical runtime instrumentation catalog for the serving runtime, the metric and trace contracts teams must follow, and an investigation playbook for the most common performance incidents. It merges runtime architecture signal expectations, kernel scheduler hooks, profiling runbooks, and how the benchmarking suite should be used to validate instrumentation changes.

Scope and audience
- Audience: runtime engineers, SREs, profiling engineers, and release owners who change execution, kernels, or observability.
- Scope: production and canary environments for Redwood Inference hosting and Dedicated clusters. Does not cover client SDK metrics.

Key goals
- Provide a small, stable set of metric and trace contracts that are cheap to collect and sufficient for SLO ownership.
- Standardize kernel-level signals that scheduler engineers must expose to telemetry.
- Offer a reproducible profiling and benchmarking workflow for validating changes to instrumentation and scheduler behavior.
- Provide step-by-step incident triage for tail latency and kernel hang patterns.

Metric and trace contract catalog (single-table view)
Note: this table is the ground truth for dashboards, SLOs, alerts, and benchmarking assertions. Keep stable names; rename only via ADR and release notes.

| Service | Metric name | Interpretation | Owner | SLI window | SLO | Alert threshold |
| Serving Runtime | runtime.request.p95_ms | p95 end-to-end runtime request latency excluding queue time | runtime-observability | 5m | p95 < 120 ms | p95 > 250 ms for 3m |
| Serving Runtime | runtime.kvcache.hit_rate | fraction of token-level KV cache hits | runtime-cache | 1h | > 0.75 across traffic | drop > 0.15 relative to baseline in 15m |
| Kernel Dispatcher | kernel.dispatch.utilization | GPU kernel dispatch utilization (0-1) | kernel-scheduler | 5m | 0.35-0.85 is healthy | sustained > 0.95 or < 0.15 for 10m |
| Kernel Dispatcher | kernel.preempt.count | number of cooperative preemptions per minute | kernel-scheduler | 1h | < 5/min averaged | > 20/min in 10m |
| Network | grpc.connection.reuse_rate | fraction of reused connections | infra-network | 1h | > 0.8 | drop below 0.5 for 30m |

Instrumentation guidance and conventions
- Metric naming: dot-separated domain.prefix.metric. Use lower case and underscores only for labels.
- Units: always append units in metric descriptions (ms, bytes, percent). Avoid unitless counters unless absolute counts.
- Cardinality: labels are limited to runtime, model_family, model_variant, region. Do not introduce free-form user identifiers.
- Sampling: traces default to 0.5% in production; increase to 2% on canaries. For kernel events, use deterministic sampling for error paths and probabilistic sampling for happy-path events.
- Baggage and spans: top-level span name must be request_id. Span tags: model, sequence_length, route.

Kernel scheduler signals and hooks
- Exposed signals: kernel.dispatch.start, kernel.dispatch.end, kernel.kernel_hint (quantization_level, preferred_slice), kernel.kvcache.prefetch_hits, kernel.handoff.reason.
- Hook semantics: kernel.dispatch.start must be emitted before any GPU work. kernel.dispatch.end must include kernel.wall_ms and kernel.tokens_produced. kernel.handoff.reason must be one of: preemption, eviction, migration, thermal_throttle.
- Backpressure indicator: runtime.queue.depth_by_priority. Use this with kernel.dispatch.utilization to compute admission decisions.

Profiling playbook: when and how to profile
1) Trigger conditions
   - Regression alert fires for runtime.request.p95_ms or kernel.dispatch.utilization anomalies.
   - Release candidate that introduces kernel or scheduler code.
2) Safe sampling plan
   - Start with live sample at 0.5% using tracing agent. Collect 10k requests or 1 hour minimum.
   - For kernel-level deep samples, schedule a controlled profiling job on canaries with overlay traffic at 10% of production QPS.
3) Commands and artifacts to collect
   - tcpdump and connection logs around the incident window (if networking suspected).
   - Kernel traces: enable kernel hook logging level 3 and collect 60s of GPU metrics via nvidia-smi or platform agent.
   - Use the profiling harness: ./tools/profiler/run_sampled_capture --trace-rate 0.01 --duration 3600 --tag regression-YYYYMMDD
4) Analysis checklist
   - Decompose latency by span: pre-queue, queue, kernel dispatch, post-process. If kernel dispatch dominates, open kernel investigation.
   - Correlate kvcache.hit_rate drops with sequence length changes.
   - Look for sudden increases in kernel.preempt.count or kernel.handoff.reason=thermal_throttle.

Benchmarking suite integration
- Purpose: validate that instrumentation changes do not skew SLOs or increase overhead beyond threshold.
- Baseline rules: every PR that changes metric emission or adds tags must run the microbenchmark suite that asserts per-token CPU overhead < 1.2x baseline and p95 latency variance < 5%.
- Synthetic corpus: use workload lanes defined in workloads/catalog.yaml where lanes include short-chat, long-infer, embedding-batch. Always run short-chat and long-infer.
- Representative test matrix: model families (small, medium, large), sequence lengths (32, 256, 1024), batch shapes (1x1, 8x8).

Release notes snippet (example for instrumentation changes)
- v2.4.0-instrumentation: Added kernel.handoff.reason field and reduced default trace sampling to 0.5% in prod. Backwards compatibility: dashboards continue to read runtime.request.p95_ms. Migration: update any alert rules that used deprecated tag "kernel_phase".

Known issues and guidance
- Issue: transient kvcache hit_rate drop on warm startups. Workaround: enable kvcache.warmup_hint for canaries to prefetch top 10k prefixes.
- Issue: occasional nvlink interconnect flapping shows as kernel.dispatch.utilization oscillation. Guidance: treat as infra/networking incident and escalate to infra-network team.
- Issue: high preemption counts after scheduler changes. If kernel.preempt.count > 20/min, rollback scheduler commit or apply temporary admission controller to reduce concurrency by 30%.

Incident triage playbook: high tail latency (p95 spike)
Step 0: Declare incident if p95 > 250 ms for 3 consecutive minutes and SLO burn expected. Notify oncall and post to channel #runtime-incident.
Step 1: Immediately check top-line signals
   - runtime.request.p95_ms, runtime.request.error_rate, kernel.dispatch.utilization, runtime.queue.depth_by_priority
Step 2: Narrow to span that increased
   - Use trace sample drilldown to find whether queue or kernel dispatch increased. If queue increased, jump to Step 4. If kernel dispatch increased, go to Step 3.
Step 3: Kernel investigation
   - Check kernel.preempt.count, kernel.handoff.reason, kernel.kernel_hint distributions.
   - If preemptions are high, run a canary with reduced concurrency. If handoffs show thermal_throttle, open hardware ops ticket.
Step 4: Queue and admission control
   - Inspect request arrival rate and admission controller logs.
   - If backpressure misconfiguration suspected, apply emergency admission policy: reject low-priority routes and reduce max tokens per request by 20%.
Step 5: Mitigation and rollback
   - If a recent deploy is implicated, follow the runtime deployment circuit breaker and rollback matrix. If not, apply temporary circuit breakers and schedule deeper profiling.
Step 6: Postmortem
   - Fill incident template: impact, root cause hypothesis, timeline, remediation, monitoring changes, action items. Assign a 2-week follow-up for regression test addition.

Ownership and escalation
- Primary oncall: runtime SRE rotation. Secondary: kernel-scheduler rotation. Tertiary: infra-network oncall.
- Pager duty runbook link: docs/pagerduty-runtime (internal link).

Appendix: common CLI snippets
- Quick latency decomposition using trace sampler: curl -X POST https://canary-api.internal/trace/decompose -d '{ request_id: R123 }'
- Start a controlled profiling capture on canary: ./tools/profiler/start_capture --env canary --tag perf-capture --duration 300

Document maintenance
- This document is the central catalog for metric and kernel signal contracts. Any change to names, units, or cardinality requires an ADR and a release-note entry.
- Owner: runtime-observability. Review cadence: quarterly or ahead of any major scheduler release.
